pages.text: "There's a shell! I'll get it!" Pongi looked into the water from the bank in spring. One shell lay still on the bottom. Her little brother held his shell and looked in beside her.
Splash! Pongi jumped into the water. She stretched out her paws, but a ripple slid the shell away. Her paws gripped only empty water.
She jumped in five times and missed all five. Pongi climbed onto the bank and plopped down. "I can't... I don't want the shell anymore." Her mouth drooped.
Dad, in his overalls, walked along the bank and sat beside Pongi. "It's like that for everyone at first. I missed ten times long ago." Her brother nodded, hugging his shell.
Dad quietly told her, "Stop right above the shell. Then cover it with both paws at once." He put his paws together to show her. Pongi copied him.
Pongi jumped in again. Splash! She popped her head out with a puff of air. "It slipped away, but I touched it!" Dad sang from the bank, "Splash in, then splash again!"
Another splash! She came up with empty paws again. But her mouth didn't droop. "It's all right. Splash in, then splash again!" She took a big breath on the surface and went under again.
Pongi climbed onto the bank and opened her paws. There was the shell! She had stopped above it and covered it with both paws. "Got it!" She thumped her tail. Her brother hopped. "Sis!"

All three put their paws together and made a promise. "One, it's all right if it doesn't work! Two, stop above it and cover it! Three, splash in, then splash again!" Over their joined paws, Pongi called, "Next time I'll catch an even bigger shell!"
Dad hugged Pongi tight. "You kept jumping in after you missed. Wonderful, Pongi!" Even after five misses, the sixth try might work. Pongi raised her shell. "Splash in, then splash again!"
